test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 4 March 2023)
subject: general
question: If two large samples are drawn independently from two populations, then which of the following test statistic will be appropriate for testing the significance of difference of two proportions?
solution:
The correct answer is **z-test. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• If two large samples are drawn independently from two populations and we want to test the significance of the difference in proportions between the two populations, the appropriate test statistic is the Z-test.
 
 
• The Z-test is used to compare the difference between two proportions when the sample sizes are large. It is based on the assumption that the sampling distribution of the difference in proportions can be approximated by a normal distribution. 
 
• The Z-test calculates the test statistic by comparing the observed difference in proportions to the expected difference under the null hypothesis. The test statistic is then compared to the critical value from the standard normal distribution to determine the statistical significance of the difference.
 
 
 
• 
 
The test statistic is a z-score (z) defined by the following equation is z = {{(p−P)} over σ}; where, P is the hypothesized value of population proportion in the null hypothesis, p is the sample proportion and σ is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution. 

 
 
• 
 
The formula for the Z-test statistic for comparing two proportions is z = {{ ρ - P₀} over sqrt {P₀ (1 - P₀) over n}} ; where, n = sample size, ρ = observed proportion and P0 is the null hypothesis. 

 
 
• If the absolute value of the calculated Z-test statistic exceeds the critical value from the standard normal distribution, it indicates a significant difference between the two proportions.

**Hence, in the case of testing the significance of the difference in proportions between two large independent samples, the appropriate test statistic is the Z-test.**
